task_instance: Triage a small backlog of three backend tickets (a session-token-refresh ticket, a legacy-endpoint-deletion ticket, and a cloud-console WAF ticket) against a sample repo: verify each against the code, classify into done/stale/open/partial, then close the clearly-done one with an evidence comment and move it to a closed workflow state, as the skill prescribes.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is acting on Linear issues: step 2 requires listing and reading issues through Linear tools, and steps 5-6 require adding an evidence comment and moving each closed issue to a closed workflow state in Linear. This office-assistant runtime grants only text-file read/write and web access; it has no Linear issue-management tool, so the issue surface cannot be loaded and no comment or state change can be written. The hosted Linear connector is also unavailable and the safety rules forbid calling any connector tool. Without Linear there is no way to perform or verify the deliverable; the code-verification and classification steps alone do not constitute the skill's output.
evidence: Read the skill at skills/r021/skills/linear-ticket-triage/SKILL.md (requires Linear tools for listing issues and for commenting + moving issues to closed states). Built a minimal realistic input: sample_repo/auth/session.py (implements refresh_session_token, evidence that BAC-101 is Done) and sample_tickets.json (BAC-101 Done, BAC-102 still-open legacy-deletion, BAC-103 no-longer-relevant console/WAF config). Classification against the sample code is doable with file reads, but the deliverable actions — loading real Linear issues, posting an evidence comment, and transitioning an issue to a closed state — have no available tool in this runtime and are forbidden by the safety rules, so the triage cannot be executed or verified. Files produced: sample_repo/auth/session.py, sample_tickets.json, result.json (all under the r021 work directory).
